body.text: śrīmatām utkarṣaparijñānād vaidagdhyena sahṛdayatvān nāgarikatāsiddhiḥ / yuvatyādīnām utkarṣo dehe\var{dehe\lem \ed; deha# \ka} guṇālaṅkārajīvitaparikarebhyaḥ / tatra śobhāvidhāyino dharmā guṇāḥ /
body.translated_text: The accomplishment of urbanity (<s>nāgarikatā</s>) is achieved through expertise arising from the recognition of the excellence of the distinguished, and from being a <s>sahṛdaya</s> (connoisseur, literally 'one who has heart'). The excellence of young women and the like consists of the body, good qualities (<s>guṇas</s>), ornaments, and life's accompaniments. Among these, the qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) are the properties that bestow beauty.

body.text:
1ab: rūpaṃ varṇaḥ prabhā rāga & ābhijātyaṃ vilāsitā
1cd: lāvaṇyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ chāyā & saubhāgyaṃ cety amī guṇāḥ
body.translated_text:
Verse 1ab: Form (<s>rūpa</s>), complexion (<s>varṇa</s>), radiance (<s>prabhā</s>), passion (<s>rāga</s>), and nobility (<s>ābhijātya</s>), coquetry (<s>vilāsitā</s>)
1cd: grace (<s>lāvaṇya</s>), [auspicious] mark (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), charm (<s>chāyā</s>), and good fortune (<s>saubhāgya</s>) — these are the qualities.

body.text: avayavānāṃ rekhāspāṣṭyaṃ rūpaṃ / gauratādidharmaviśeṣo varṇaḥ / kācakācyarūpā\var{kācakācya#\lem \ed; kācakacya# \kha} ravivatkāntiḥ prabhā / naisargika\var{naisargika#\lem \ed; naisargikaḥ \kha}smeratvamukhaprasādādiḥ sarveṣām eva cakṣurbandhako dharmo rāgaḥ / kusumadharmā mārdavādir lālanādirūpaḥ sparśaviśeṣaḥ peśalatākhya ābhijātyam / aṅgopāṅgānāṃ yauvanodbhedī manmathavāsanāprayuktaḥ kaṭākṣādivadvibhramākhyaś ceṣṭāviśeṣo vilāsitā / taraṅgidravasvabhāvāpyāyinetrapeyavyāpisnigdhamadhura iva pītimotkarṣaikasāra iva pūrṇenduvadāhlādako dharmaḥ saṃsthānamugdhimavyaṅgyo lāvaṇyam / aṅgopāṅgānām asādhāraṇaśobhāprāśastyahetur aucityātmā sthāyī dharmo lakṣaṇam / tasya yuktapramāṇatādoṣasparśasnigdhavaktraniyatalomāṅgasuśliṣṭasaṃdhānatānāhapariṇāhaucityacakrapadmādilekhāṅkanāyogebhyaḥ prasiddhāṅgapūrṇatādoṣavaikalyadharmasaundaryapramāṇaucityalokāprasiddhaviśiṣṭāṅgayogākhyāḥ krameṇa ṣaḍ bhedāḥ / agrāmyatayā vakrimatvakhyāpinī tāmbūlaparidhānanṛttabhaṇitigamanādisthānakeṣu sūkṣmā bhaṅgiś chāyā / sphurallakṣmyupabhogaparimalādigamyo 'ntaḥsāro rañjakatayā vaśīkartā sahṛdayasaṃvedyadharmabhedaś ca saubhāgyam / tatrādye smaramadapulakādayo bhedāḥ antye tu maṇita+rūpa+paribhoga+adhara+āsvāda+saurabha+ādibhir yugapad+rasavattvāt pañca+indriya+sukha+lābhaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (form) is the clarity of lines of the limbs. <s>Varṇa</s> (complexion) is a particular quality like fairness and the rest. <s>Prabhā</s> (radiance) is a brilliance of the nature of shimmering glass-like luster, like that of the sun. <s>Rāga</s> (passion) is a naturally smiling, pleasing-faced and similar quality that is a charmer of the eyes of everyone. <s>Ābhijātya</s> (nobility) — also called <s>peśalatā</s> — is a specific touch like the flower's property of softness, tenderness, and caressibility. <s>Vilāsitā</s> (coquetry) is a particular movement like a sidelong glance, which is [named] <s>vibhrama</s> (amorous gesture), roused by the perfume of the god of love (<s>manmatha</s>), erupting with the bloom of youth in the minor and major limbs. <s>Lāvaṇya</s> (grace) is a quality that is charming like the configuration of an innocent [face], impossible to express by secondary indication, delighting like a full moon, as if essential in the single essence of the highest delight, with eyes drinking it as if it were wave-flowing by nature and pervading as if sweet smooth liquid. <s>Lakṣaṇa</s> (auspicious mark) is a permanent quality that is the cause of the uncommon beauty-excellence of the major and minor limbs, consisting in propriety; it has six subtypes in order: completeness of famous limbs, defect-freedom, beauty, correct proportion, propriety, and the named possession of special limbs known to the world — arising from [respectively:] correct proportion without defect-touch, the smoothness of the face, fixity of hair [lines], well-fitting joints, tautness, [appropriate] girth, the correctness of the lines of the wheel and lotus etc. <s>Chāyā</s> (charm) is a subtle curvature expressing crookedness in an ungrossly [manner] in [activities] like betel-nut [chewing], dressing, dancing, speaking, walking, and similar postures. <s>Saubhāgya</s> (good fortune) is an inner essence — attainable by shining splendor, experience, fragrance, and the like — that is a <s>dharma</s>-distinction known to connoisseurs, captivating by its infatuating [quality]. Among these, in the former [<s>rāga</s>]: the subdivisions are the erotic excitement (<s>smaramada</s>), horripilation (<s>pulaka</s>), and the rest; but in the latter [<s>saubhāgya</s>]: the attainment of pleasure for the five senses simultaneously, due to the richness of taste through jewels, form, enjoyment, savoring the lips, fragrance, and so forth.
Thus [ends] the first chapter, the enumeration of qualities (<s>guṇollekha</s>), in the <s>Sahṛdayalīlā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Rājānaka Ruyyaka</s>.

body.text:
2ab: ratnaṃ hemāṃśuke mālyaṃ & maṇḍanadravyayojane
2cd: prakīrṇaṃ cety alaṅkārāḥ & saptaiv[ai]te mayā matāḥ
body.translated_text:
Verse 2ab: Jewel (<s>ratna</s>), garment of gold-thread (<s>hemāṃśuka</s>), garland (<s>mālya</s>), combination of decorative substances (<s>maṇḍanadravyayojana</s>),
2cd: and miscellaneous (<s>prakīrṇa</s>) — these seven are the ornaments (<s>alaṅkāras</s>) as I consider them.

body.text:
tatra vajra+muktā+padmarāga+marakata+indranīla+vaidūrya+puṣparāga+karketana+pulaka+rudhira+akṣa+bhīṣma+sphaṭika+pravāla+rūpāṇi trayodaśa ratnāni / hema navadhā / jāmbūnada+śātakaumbha+hāṭaka+vaiṇava+śṛṅgī+śuktija+jātarūpa+rasaviddha+ākara+udgata+bhedāt / caturdhā ratna+hema+mayaḥ, āvedhya+nibandhanīya+prakṣepya+āropya+bhedāt / tatra tāḍī+kuṇḍala+śravaṇa+vālika+ādir āvedhyaḥ / aṅgada+śroṇīsūtra+mūrdhamaṇi+śikhādṛḍhikā+ādir nibandhanīyaḥ /
ūrmikā+kaṭaka+mañjīra+sadṛśaḥ prakṣepyaḥ / %folded, twisted (linked?), post-like/anklet-like?
prālamba+mālikā+āhāra+nakṣatramālā+prabhṛtir āropyaḥ / caturdhā+aṃśuka+mayaḥ / tvak+phala+krimi+romajatvāt krameṇa kṣauma+kārpāsa+kauśeya+rāṅkava+ādibhedāt / punas tridhā, nibandhanīya+prakṣepya+āropya+vaicitryāt / tatra nibandhanīyaḥ śirah+śāṭaka+jaghana+vasana+ādiḥ / prakṣepyaḥ kañculika+ādiḥ / āropya uttarīya+paṭa+ādiḥ / sarvasya+ asya+ anekavidhatvaṃ varṇa+vicchitti+nānātvāt / grathita+agrathita+vaśād dvividhaḥ sann aṣṭadhā mālya+mayaḥ / veṣṭita+vitata+saṃghāṭya+granthimad+avalamba+muktaka+mañjīra+stabaka+lakṣaṇa+mālya+bhedena / tatra+ udvartitaṃ veṣṭitam / pārśvato vistāritaṃ vitatam / bahubhiḥ puṣpaiḥ samūhena racitaṃ saṃghātyam / antarāntarā viṣamaṃ granthimat / spaṣṭombhitam (?) avalambham / kevalaṃ muktakaḥ / aneka+puṣpa+mayī latā mañjarī / kusuma+gulucchaṃ stabakaḥ / tasya+ āvedhya+ādayo 'pi catvāro bhedāḥ / kastūrī+kuṅkuma+candana+karpūra+aguru+kulaka+dantasama+paṭavāsa+sahakāra+taila+tāmbūla+alakta+kāñjana+gorocana+ādi+nirvṛtto maṇḍana+dravya+mayaḥ / bhrū+ghaṭanā+alaka+racanā+dhammilla+bandhana+ādir yojanāmayaḥ / dvidhā prakīrṇa+mayaḥ, janya+niveśya+bhedena / śrama+jala+madhu+mada+ādi+janyaḥ / dūrva+aśoka+pallava+yava+aṅkura+rajata+trapu+śaṅkha+tāla+dala+danta+pattrikā+mṛṇāla+valaya+kara+krīḍanaka+ādir niveśyaḥ / etat samavāyo veṣaḥ / sa ca deśa+kāla+prakṛti+avasthā+sātmyena / eteṣāṃ vicchityā yathā+āsthāna+niveśana+parabhāga+lābhād rāmaṇīyaka+vṛddhiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Among these, the thirteen gems are: <s>vajra</s> (diamond), <s>muktā</s> (pearl), <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby), <s>marakata</s> (emerald), <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire), <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's eye), <s>puṣparāga</s> (topaz), <s>karketana</s> (hessonite), <s>pulaka</s> (a gem type), <s>rudhirākṣa</s> (bloodstone), <s>bhīṣma</s> (a gem type), <s>sphaṭika</s> (crystal), and <s>pravāla</s> (coral). Gold is of nine kinds: distinguished as <s>jāmbūnada</s>, <s>śātakaumbha</s>, <s>hāṭaka</s>, <s>vaiṇava</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, <s>śuktija</s> (born from a shell), <s>jātarūpa</s> (naturally formed), <s>rasaviddha</s> (alchemically produced), and <s>ākarodbhūta</s> (mined from a deposit). Ornaments made of gems and gold are of four kinds, distinguished as: <s>āvedhya</s> (pierced, i.e., those worn through piercings), <s>nibandhanīya</s> (those that are tied on), <s>prakṣepya</s> (those that are slipped on), and <s>āropya</s> (those that are placed upon). Among these, <s>āvedhya</s> (pierced ornaments) include <s>tāḍī</s> (ear ornament), <s>kuṇḍala</s> (earring), <s>śravaṇa</s> (ear-piece), <s>vālikā</s> (nose-ring), and so forth. <s>Nibandhanīya</s> (tied ornaments) include <s>aṅgada</s> (armlet), <s>śroṇīsūtra</s> (hip-chain), <s>mūrdhamaṇi</s> (crest-jewel), <s>śikhādṛḍhikā</s> (hair-clasp), and so forth.
<s>Prakṣepya</s> (slipped-on ornaments) are like <s>ūrmikā</s> (finger-ring), <s>kaṭaka</s> (bracelet), <s>mañjīra</s> (anklet), and similar items.
<s>Āropya</s> (placed-upon ornaments) include <s>prālamba</s> (pendant necklace), <s>mālikā</s> (garland), <s>āhāra</s> (necklace), <s>nakṣatramālā</s> (star-garland), and so forth. Garments made of cloth are of four kinds, because they arise respectively from bark, fruit, worms (silk), and hair — thus distinguished as <s>kṣauma</s> (linen), <s>kārpāsa</s> (cotton), <s>kauśeya</s> (silk), <s>rāṅkava</s> (wool), and others. Again, these are of three kinds, due to the variety of <s>nibandhanīya</s> (tied), <s>prakṣepya</s> (put on), and <s>āropya</s> (draped). Among these, <s>nibandhanīya</s> (tied garments) include the head-cloth, <s>jaghanavasana</s> (lower garment), and so forth. <s>Prakṣepya</s> (put-on garments) include the <s>kañculikā</s> (bodice) and others. <s>Āropya</s> (draped garments) include the <s>uttarīya</s> (upper garment), shawl, and others. The manifold variety of all these arises from differences in color and design. Garlands are of eight kinds, being twofold as strung and unstrung: distinguished as <s>veṣṭita</s> (wound), <s>vitata</s> (spread out), <s>saṃghāṭya</s> (massed), <s>granthimat</s> (knotted), <s>avalamba</s> (hanging), <s>muktaka</s> (loose), <s>mañjarī</s> (clustered spray), and <s>stabaka</s> (bouquet). Among these, the <s>veṣṭita</s> is one that is wound around. The <s>vitata</s> is one spread out sideways. The <s>saṃghāṭya</s> is composed of many flowers arranged in a mass. The <s>granthimat</s> is uneven with knots at intervals. The <s>avalamba</s> is one that hangs straight down. The <s>muktaka</s> is simply loose. The <s>mañjarī</s> is a creeper-like spray made of many flowers. The <s>stabaka</s> is a cluster of blossoms. These also have four sub-varieties as pierced and so on. Cosmetic substances are produced from <s>kastūrī</s> (musk), <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), <s>karpūra</s> (camphor), <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), <s>kulaka</s>, <s>dantasama</s>, <s>paṭavāsa</s> (scented powder), <s>sahakāra</s> (mango), oils, <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), <s>alakta</s> (lac-dye), <s>kāñjana</s>, <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow pigment), and others. Arrangements consist of shaping the brows, styling the hair-locks, tying the <s>dhammilla</s> (hair-knot), and so forth. Scattered ornaments are of two kinds, distinguished as those that arise naturally and those that are placed. Natural ones arise from perspiration, honey(-like sweat), intoxication, and similar states. Placed ones include <s>dūrvā</s> (sacred grass), <s>aśoka</s> shoots, <s>yava</s> (barley) sprouts, silver ornaments, tin, conch, <s>tāla</s> (palm) leaves, tooth-ornaments, lotus-fiber bracelets, hand-toys, and so forth. The combination of all these constitutes the <s>veṣa</s> (attire/costume). And this (must accord) with region, time, nature, condition, and suitability. Through the artful arrangement of these, when placed in their proper positions, the beauty increases by gaining excellence.
Thus ends the second (chapter), the Sketch of Ornamentation (<s>alaṅkārollekha</s>), in the <s>Sahṛdayalīlā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Rājānaka Ruyyaka</s>.

body.text: śobhāyās+ anuprāṇakaṃ yauvana+ākhyaṃ jīvitam / bālya+anantaram gātrāṇāṃ vaipulya+sauṣṭhava+vibhaktatā+vidhāyī sphuṭita+dāḍima+upamaḥ smara+vasatir avasthā+bhedo yauvanam / tasya vayaḥ+saṃdhir ārambhaḥ / madhyaṃ tu prauḍhi+kālaḥ / prathame dhammilla+racanā+alaka+bhaṅga+nīvi+nahana+danta+parikarma+pariṣkaraṇa+darpaṇa+īkṣaṇa+puṣpa+uccaya+mālya+umbhana+jala+krīḍā+dyūta+aślīla+ccheka+bhaṇiti+animitta+lajjā+anubhāva+śṛṅgāra+śikṣā+ādaya āvartamānāś ceṣṭāḥ / antye tu śṛṅgāra+anubhāva+tāratamyaṃ śreyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The life-force of beauty is called youth (<s>yauvana</s>). Following childhood, (it is) the stage that brings about fullness, gracefulness, and shapeliness of limbs — compared to a split pomegranate — the abode of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), distinguished by states. Its beginning is the junction of ages (<s>vayaḥsandhi</s>). Its middle, however, is the time of maturity (<s>prauḍhi</s>). In the first (stage), the ongoing activities include: tying the <s>dhammilla</s> (hair-knot), styling the hair-curls, tying the <s>nīvi</s> (girdle-knot), attending to the teeth, adorning oneself, gazing into mirrors, gathering flowers, stringing garlands, water-sports, games, playfully immodest witty speech, causeless bashfulness, and the practices and training in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment). In the final (stage), the gradation of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> effects is considered best.
Thus ends the third (chapter), the Sketch of the Life-Force (<s>jīvitollekha</s>), in the <s>Sahṛdayalīlā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Rājānaka Ruyyaka</s>.

body.text: śobhāyās+ ārād upakārakatvād vyañjakaḥ parikaraḥ / tasya cetana+acetanayoḥ sthāṇu+calayoḥ pratyekaṃ śliṣṭa+saṃnihita+mātra+rūpatvena+ aṣṭavidhatvam / utsaṅga+upāsīna+kānta+haya+parivāra+vātāyana+vitāna+nau+cchatra+ādīni darśanāni / tāni dvidhā, vyasta+samasta+bhedāt / evaṃ śobhā+samutpādaka+samuddīpaka+anuprāṇaka+vyañjakāḥ kramād guṇa+alaṅkāra+jīvita+parikarāḥ / evaṃ paraspara+upakarakatvād itaretara+anugrāhakatvaṃ siddham /
body.translated_text: The <s>parikara</s> (retinue/accompaniment) is what indirectly assists beauty. It is of eight kinds, being of two types — sentient and insentient, stationary and moving — each through being merely closely related and proximate in form: [sights include] the lap (<s>utsaṅga</s>), attendants seated nearby (<s>upāsīna</s>), a beloved (<s>kānta</s>), a horse (<s>haya</s>), a retinue (<s>parivāra</s>), a window (<s>vātāyana</s>), a canopy (<s>vitāna</s>), a boat (<s>nau</s>), a parasol (<s>cchatra</s>), and so forth — these are the [types of] sights. They are twofold, by virtue of the distinction between separate (<s>vyasta</s>) and combined (<s>samasta</s>). Thus, in order: qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), ornaments (<s>alaṅkāra</s>), life-force (<s>jīvita</s>), and retinue (<s>parikara</s>) are the producers, inflamer, vitalizer, and expresser of beauty. Thus, because they are mutually assisting one another, their mutual supportiveness is established.
Thus ends the fourth [chapter], the Sketch of Retinue (<s>parikarollekha</s>), in the <s>Sahṛdayalīlā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Rājānaka Ruyyaka</s>.
